With C between A and B, A (same sense) attracts C towards A with mu0*I*I1/(2*pi*(r/3)) = 3*mu0*I*I1/(2*pi*r) while B (opposite sense) repels C, also towards A, with 3*mu0*I*I1/(4*pi*r); the two add to 9*mu0*I*I1/(4*pi*r) towards A. questions.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
questions.context: A pure semiconductor like Ge or Si, when doped with a small amount of suitable impurity, becomes an extrinsic semiconductor. In thermal equilibrium, the electron and hole concentration in it are related to the concentration of intrinsic charge carriers. A p-type or n-type semiconductor can be converted into a p-n junction by doping it with suitable impurity. Two processes, diffusion and drift take place during formation of a p-n junction. A semiconductor diode is basically a p-n junction with metallic contacts provided at the ends for the application of an external voltage. A p-n junction diode allows currents to pass only in one direction when it is forward biased. Due to this property, a diode is widely used to rectify alternating voltages, in half-wave or full wave configuration.

questions.context: A lens is a transparent optical medium bounded by two surfaces; at least one of which should be spherical. Applying the formula of image formation by a single spherical surface successively at the two surfaces of a thin lens, a formula known as lens maker's formula and hence the basic lens formula can be obtained. The focal length (or power) of a lens depends on the radii of its surfaces and the refractive index of its material with respect to the surrounding medium. The refractive index of a material depends on the wavelength of light used. Combination of lenses helps us to obtain diverging or converging lenses of desired power and magnification.
questions.stem: The focal length of an equiconvex lens

options.label: A
options.text: increases when the lens is dipped in water.

options.label: B
options.text: increases when the wavelength of incident light decreases.

options.label: C
options.text: increases with decrease in radius of curvature of its surface.

options.label: D
options.text: decreases when the lens is cut into two identical parts along its principal axis.

questions.stem: A thin convex lens L of focal length 10 cm and a concave mirror M of focal length 15 cm are placed coaxially 40 cm apart as shown in figure. A beam of light coming parallel to the principal axis is incident on the lens. The final image will be formed at a distance of
questions._figure: REQUIRED — every option is expressed as 'left of lens' or 'right of lens', and which way is left is fixed only by the drawn direction of the incoming beam. Described here without stating the result: a horizontal dashed principal axis; a biconvex lens labelled L drawn on the left with four horizontal ray arrows approaching it; a concave mirror labelled M drawn on the right with its reflecting side facing the lens; and the lens-to-mirror separation marked 40 cm by a double-headed arrow. Page idx 18.
questions._flag: READING NOTE (key retained, not disputed) — CBSE's (B) is the image the concave mirror forms, which sits 30 cm in front of the mirror, i.e. 10 cm to the right of the lens. Taken strictly, the converging beam then passes that point, diverges, reaches the lens as a real object 10 cm away and emerges parallel, so a fully literal 'final image' would be at infinity; no option offers that, so (B) is plainly the intended reading and is kept.

(ii) Two capacitors of different capacitances are connected first (1) in series and then (2) in parallel across a dc source of 100 V. If the total energy stored in the combination in the two cases are 40 mJ and 250 mJ respectively, find the capacitance of the capacitors.

(i) Using Gauss's law, show that the electric field \(\vec{E}\) at a point due to a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet is given by \(\vec{E} = \dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\hat{n}\) where symbols have their usual meanings.
(ii) Electric field \(\vec{E}\) in a region is given by
\(\vec{E} = (5x^2 + 2)\hat{i}\)
where E is in N/C and \(x\) is in meters.
A cube of side 10 cm is placed in the region as shown in figure.
Calculate (1) the electric flux through the cube, and (2) the net charge enclosed by the cube.
questions._figure: REQUIRED for sub-part (ii) — the flux depends on WHERE along the x-axis the cube sits and how its faces are oriented, and the stem says only 'as shown in figure'. What is drawn: a right-handed axis triad with y up, x to the right and z toward the lower-left; a cube drawn in oblique projection with one vertex at the marked origin 0 and its edges parallel to the three axes; and, to the right of the cube, an arrow labelled \(\vec{E}\) with a second arrow labelled \(\hat{i}\) beneath it, both pointing along \(+x\). questions.stem:
(i) Draw a ray diagram for the formation of the image of an object by a convex mirror. Hence, obtain the mirror equation.
(ii) Why are multi-component lenses used for both the objective and the eyepiece in optical instruments ?
(iii) The magnification of a small object produced by a compound microscope is 200. The focal length of the eyepiece is 2 cm and the final image is formed at infinity. Find the magnification produced by the objective.
questions._flag: MIXED SUBTOPIC — sub-part (i) is 'Reflection by Spherical Mirrors' while (ii) and (iii) are 'Optical Instruments'. Filed on the majority, 'Optical Instruments'.

questions.stem:
(i) Differentiate between a wavefront and a ray.
(ii) State Huygen's principle and verify laws of reflection using suitable diagram.
(iii) In Young's double slit experiment, the slits \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) are 3 mm apart and the screen is placed 1.0 m away from the slits. It is observed that the fourth bright fringe is at a distance of 5 mm from the second dark fringe. Find the wavelength of light used.
questions._flag: MIXED SUBTOPIC — sub-parts (i) and (ii) are 'Huygens Principle' while (iii) is 'Interference and Young's Experiment'. Filed on the majority, 'Huygens Principle'. SEPARATE OBSERVATION on sub-part (iii): the printed data give an unphysical wavelength. With d = 3 mm and D = 1.0 m, the fourth bright fringe and the second dark fringe are separated by 2.5*D*lambda/d, so 5 mm implies lambda = 6e-6 m = 6 micrometre, which is infrared rather than visible light. The marking scheme derives and accepts exactly that value, so the stem is transcribed as printed and the number is NOT corrected.
